title: The CAGED System
intro: The five open major chords C, A, G, E and D are also five movable shapes. Slid up the neck in that order, each one joins the next, so together they map every chord tone of a major chord across the whole fretboard.

blocks.text: Play a C major chord in open position (the C shape, x32010). Now find the next C major up the neck: the A shape barred at fret 3 (x35553). Then the G shape around fret 5 (8-7-5-5-5-8), the E shape barred at fret 8 (8-10-10-9-8-8) and the D shape around fret 10 (x-x-10-12-13-12). After the D shape comes the C shape again, an octave up at fret 12. The order C–A–G–E–D repeats endlessly, starting from whichever shape your key's open chord is.

widget.title: C major in all five CAGED shapes

blocks.text: Each shape contains roots, thirds and fifths in fixed places, so CAGED is really a map of where the root, 3rd and 5th of a major chord are. Lower each 3rd by a fret and the five shapes become the five minor shapes; add the 7th and they become seventh-chord shapes.

items: Find any chord in five places: put its root where the shape's root is. For F with the E shape, root on string 6 fret 1: the F barre chord. For F with the A shape: root on string 5 fret 8.
Link scales to chords: each CAGED shape sits inside one of the five major-scale positions and one of the five pentatonic boxes. Playing a solo 'around the shape' keeps chord tones under your fingers.
Arpeggios: play the notes of a shape one at a time for an arpeggio in that position (see Soloing over Chords (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/soloing)).

blocks.text: Many teachers prefer not to drill CAGED as rigid shapes but to use it as a map of chord tones. Either way the idea is the same: every chord exists in five overlapping places on the neck.

blocks.title: Shapes for G
blocks.text: Which CAGED shape gives G major with its root on string 5 fret 10, and which shape is the open G chord's neighbour above it?
solution: A root on string 5 is the A shape (or C shape); at fret 10 with the barre there, it is the A shape: x-10-12-12-12-10.
The order is C–A–G–E–D–C. The open G chord is the G shape; the next shape up is the E shape, barred at fret 3 (3-5-5-4-3-3).
blocks.answer: A shape at fret 10; next up from open G is the E shape at fret 3

blocks.text: Sources: Goodrick, M. (1987). The Advancing Guitarist. Hal Leonard; Wyatt, K. & Schroeder, C. (1998). Harmony and Theory: A Comprehensive Source for All Musicians. Hal Leonard; Tagliarino, B. (2006). Guitar Fretboard Workbook. Hal Leonard.
